analysis.reason: This paper focuses strictly on gravitational-wave ringdown theory and quasinormal mode (QNM) convergence in black hole perturbation theory, which falls outside our core transient astrophysics interests (such as FRB/PRS, supernovae, relativistic jets, and high-energy observations).
analysis.result: The start time of ringdown for a constant-amplitude QNM expansion is mathematically determined by the advanced time $v_S$ at which the worldline continued into the black hole reaches the singularity $r=0$, giving $u_S = v_S$. The delay relative to the bounce time $u_B$ is analytically given by $$u_S - u_B = v_S - v_B = \int_0^{r_B} \mathrm{d}r\, \frac{1+L^2/r^2}{\sqrt{R(r)}(E+\sqrt{R(r)})}$$, which yields $u_S \simeq u_B + 3.37M \simeq u_{\rm peak} + 9.4M$ for an ISCO plunge and $u_S \simeq u_B + 0.87M$ for radial free-fall. Prior to $u_S$, the constant-amplitude sum diverges, whereas for $u > u_S$ it converges exponentially as $e^{-|{\rm Im}\,\omega_n|(u-u_S)}$.
analysis.problem: Resolving the mathematical ambiguity and physical origin of the start time $t_S$ of gravitational wave ringdown, specifically explaining why a constant-amplitude quasinormal mode (QNM) sum fails to converge immediately after the waveform peak or horizon crossing.
analysis.method: Solving the Regge-Wheeler and Zerilli perturbation equations $(\partial_t^2 - \partial_x^2 + V)\Psi = S(t,x)$ for a point particle falling into a Schwarzschild black hole using hyperboloidal slicing, combined with a Green function decomposition into dynamical QNM amplitudes $C_n(u)$ and regularized constant amplitudes $\tilde{C}_n$ expanded near the horizon Kruskal coordinate $U = -e^{-u/2}$ up to overtone number $n=150$.
citation_leads: The Start Time of Ringdown: “While a dynamical amplitude model reproduces the waveform after the particle crosses the bounce radius, a constant amplitude sum converges only after the start time $t_{S}$, which corresponds to the advanced time at which the particle hits”

The Start Time of Ringdown: “The constant-amplitude sum behaves differently. Its convergence is set by the singularity of the source nearest to $U=0$ of the source along the worldline, continued into the BH: this corresponds to $r=0$.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that the waveform after the particle crosses the bounce radius $u_B$ is completely captured by dynamical QNM amplitudes, whereas constant-amplitude QNM sums are strictly divergent until $u_S$, with convergence set by analytic continuation to the $r=0$ singularity rather than horizon-scale geometry.

analysis.reason: The paper provides an ultra-precise measurement of the supermassive black hole mass in M87 using combined JWST NIRSpec and Keck KCWI stellar kinematics with triaxial Schwarzschild modeling, providing a critical gravitational anchor and prior for horizon-scale EHT observations and relativistic jet launch physics.
analysis.result: The triaxial orbit modeling determines the central black hole mass to be $M_{\mathrm{BH}} = (5.38 \pm 0.13 \pm 0.22) \times 10^{9}\,M_{\odot}$ (with the second uncertainty from the distance $D = 16.8 \pm 0.7\,\mathrm{Mpc}$), corresponding to an angular gravitational radius $\theta_g \equiv GM_{\mathrm{BH}}/(c^2 D) = 3.16 \pm 0.08\,\mu\mathrm{as}$. The dark matter mass within $10\,\mathrm{kpc}$ is $M_{\mathrm{DM}}(<10\,\mathrm{kpc}) = (3.57 \pm 0.10 \pm 0.15) \times 10^{11}\,M_{\odot}$, and the intrinsic triaxial shape parameter is $T = 0.59 \pm 0.01$.
analysis.reading_entry: V.1 Black Hole Mass, Stellar Mass, and Dark Matter Halo Mass
analysis.problem: Resolving long-standing discrepancies in the black hole mass of M87 derived from stellar dynamics, ionized gas dynamics ($(2.5\text{--}4) \times 10^9\,M_\odot$), and EHT horizon-scale shadow observations, while correcting for detector undersampling 'wiggle' artifacts in JWST NIRSpec IFU data.
analysis.method: Combining wide-field Keck KCWI and central JWST NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy covering 10 pc to 10 kpc, applying a new de-wiggling algorithm 'hyphen' with form $\mathcal{O}_{i} \approx \gamma_{i}\mathcal{F} + (1 + w_{i}\beta_{i})\alpha_{i}\mathcal{P}$ to remove detector aliasing artifacts, extracting 8 Gauss-Hermite velocity moments across 618 bins, and conducting triaxial Schwarzschild orbit modeling via TriOS with Deep Ensembles parameter inference.

analysis.reason: This study resolves the nuclear gas and stellar kinematics in eight prototypical low-luminosity AGNs with JWST/NIRSpec IFU, providing crucial empirical benchmarks for relativistic jet-ISM interactions, shock heating, and coronal line photoionization around supermassive black holes.
analysis.result: Across eight LLAGNs with $M_{\rm BH} \sim 10^{5.5-9.8}\,M_\odot$ and $\log(L_{\rm bol}/L_{\rm Edd}) \approx -6$ to $-2.7$, molecular gas ($\mathrm{H}_2$) is generally kinematically cooler and rotation-dominated compared to stars, but displays kinematic PA decoupling in M81, M94, NGC 1052, and NGC 5128. Nuclear line ratios $\mathrm{H}_2\,1\text{--}0\,\mathrm{S}(1)/\mathrm{Br}\gamma$ average $\approx 1.6$, indicating AGN photoionization dominates the parsec-scale energetics, while mechanical shock heating and enhanced dispersions occur along relativistic radio jets (e.g., reaching $\sigma \sim 700\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in M87 and $\sigma \approx 450\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in NGC 1052). Spatially resolved kinematics of high-ionization coronal lines ($[\mathrm{Si\;VI}]\,1.96\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, $[\mathrm{Mg\;VIII}]\,3.02\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, $[\mathrm{Ar\;VI}]\,4.52\,\mu\mathrm{m}$) align directly with the radio jet in NGC 5128 ($\mathrm{PA} \sim 97^\circ$) and NGC 4395.
analysis.reading_entry: 3 ReveaLLAGN: Stellar & Gas Kinematics, Flux and Excitation Maps
analysis.problem: Unveiling the parsec-scale feeding and feedback mechanisms (jet-driven shocks vs. photoionization) in RIAF-dominated LLAGNs at very low Eddington ratios, while overcoming severe sinusoidal undersampling artifacts in JWST/NIRSpec IFU data.
analysis.method: Utilized JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations in high-resolution grating modes (G235H/F170LP and G395H/F290LP, spanning $0.6\text{--}5.3\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ with $R \approx 2700$), applied WICKED to correct PSF undersampling sinusoidal wiggles, performed Voronoi spatial binning, and extracted stellar and gas kinematics via pPXF modeling of $^{12}\mathrm{CO}(2\text{--}0)$ at $2.29\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, warm $\mathrm{H}_2$, hydrogen recombination lines ($\mathrm{Pa}\alpha$, $\mathrm{Br}\gamma$), and coronal emission lines.
limits: Spatially resolved kinematics of high-ionization coronal lines were only attainable in NGC 5128 and NGC 4395, the two sources with the highest Eddington ratios.
citation_leads: 1 Introduction: “The ReveaLLAGN sample comprises eight prototypical systems with Eddington ratios from $\log(L_{bol}/L_{Edd})\approx-6$ to $\approx-2.7$ and distances of $\sim 4-20$ Mpc”
2.2 Wiggle correction: “All data cubes present substantial sinusoidal modulations in the spectra at the single-spaxel level. This is a known consequence of PSF undersampling in NIRSpec”

3 ReveaLLAGN: Stellar & Gas Kinematics, Flux and Excitation Maps: “These coronal lines arise from regions within a few parsecs of the central SMBH and are considered unambiguous signatures of AGN photoionization”
3.3 Flux and line ratios maps: “In addition to the kinematics we also present the distribution of line intensities and ratios in the nuclear regions.”
3.7 M81: “The velocity dispersion of the molecular gas is generally low across the field-of-view, with a central peak of $\sigma\approx 90$ km s-1.”
3.10 NGC 5128: “Out of the full sample, NGC 5128 and NGC 4395 are the only galaxies where we can obtain kinematics for coronal lines.”
analysis.research_progress: Provides the first spatially resolved parsec-scale infrared IFU dissection of both warm molecular and coronal gas across prototypical nearby LLAGNs, establishing direct observational mapping between relativistic jet propagation and localized kinetic energy injection into the interstellar medium.

The first three panels show the LOS velocity and the last two the velocity dispersion. The dashed black line shows the best-fit gas kinematic PA. The solid white line marks the direction of the radio jet. The dashed fuchsia line shows the stellar kinematic PA.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: Maps the molecular hydrogen and hydrogen recombination-line velocities and velocity dispersions, comparing the gas kinematic position angle with the stellar kinematic position angle and radio-jet direction.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Flux and line ratio maps. The left three panels show the flux maps for the H 2 1-0 S(1), $Pa\alpha$, and Br $\gamma$ lines. The right two panels show the H 2 /Br $\gamma$ line ratio map and a colorized version highlighting the different excitation mechanism. Values of H 2 /Br $\gamma\leq 0.4$ (blue) indicate star forming regions, $0.4 2 /Br $\gamma\leq 2.0$ low-AGN excitation (orange), $2.0 2 /Br $\gamma\leq 6.0$ high-AGN and H 2 /Br $\gamma$ above 6.0 shock excitation (green). The white line shows the direction of the radio jet.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: Shows flux maps for H₂ 1-0 S(1), Paα, and Brγ, alongside H₂/Brγ line-ratio maps used to distinguish excitation regimes, including AGN- and shock-excitation ranges.

analysis.result: The neural operator accelerates rotating relativistic star solutions by a factor of $\sim 10^3\times$ (reducing computation time from $45\,\mathrm{s}$ with traditional RNS solvers to $35\,\mathrm{ms}$, a $1283\times$ speed-up) while maintaining high fidelity, with stellar mass errors $|\Delta M| \sim 0.14\%$ and equatorial radius errors $|\Delta R| \sim 0.03\%$, enabling rigorous Bayesian MCMC EoS inference over rotating pulsar populations like PSR J0952$-$0607 ($M=2.35\pm 0.17\,M_{\odot}$, $\nu=707.3\,\mathrm{Hz}$).

analysis.problem: Traditional numerical solvers for rapidly rotating relativistic stars (e.g. iterative Green's function relaxation methods) are computationally prohibitive for large-scale Bayesian EoS parameter inference and population synthesis, whereas adopting non-rotating TOV models or low-order perturbative approximations introduces severe systematic biases.

analysis.reason: This work uncovers the physical chronology of the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (KHI) kinematic dynamo in binary neutron star mergers, showing that the dynamo is not standard turbulence-driven because asymptotic growth rates become independent of $\mathrm{Re}$, mediated instead by secondary Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI).
analysis.result: The KHI dynamo operates across three stages: Stage 1 shear winding produces a flat spectrum $E_{\rm mag}(k) \propto k^{0}$ with energy scaling $E_{\rm wound,peak}/E_{\rm mag,0} \propto \mathrm{Pm}_{\Delta}^{2/3}$. Secondary centrifugal RTI then disrupts the vortices with growth rate $\gamma_{\rm RTI}^{\infty}t_{\Delta} = \frac{3}{4^{4/3}}[\frac{Ag_{\rm eff}\delta_{0}}{(\Delta U)^{2}}]^{2/3}\mathrm{Re}_{\Delta}^{1/3}$, imposing a dynamo onset delay $t_{\rm delay}/t_{\Delta} \propto \mathrm{Re}_{\Delta}^{-1/3}$. At high Reynolds numbers ($\,\mathrm{Re}_\Delta \ge 512$), the kinematic growth rate saturates to an $\mathrm{Re}$-independent value $\gamma_{E}t_{\Delta} \sim 0.02$ (yielding $\gamma_E \simeq 36\,\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ for BNS parameters) with a Kazantsev spectrum $E_{\rm mag}(k) \propto k^{3/2}$, directly amplifying mean vertical fields to $\overline{B}_{z} \sim 10^{14}\text{--}10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ at an unresolvable microscopic scale $\lambda_{\rm RTI}^{\infty} \approx 6\,\mathrm{cm}$.
analysis.problem: Global binary neutron star merger simulations observe magnetic field amplification at shear interfaces but suffer from numerical dissipation; whether the amplification is a standard small-scale turbulent dynamo with growth rate $\gamma_E \propto \mathrm{Re}^{1/2}$ or driven by resolved shear winding remained controversial.
analysis.method: Direct numerical simulations of 3D compressible Newtonian viscous-resistive MHD using AthenaK on triply periodic domains ($1152^3\text{--}2304^3$ grid cells) covering $64 \le \mathrm{Re}_{\Delta} \le 16384$, magnetic Prandtl numbers $\mathrm{Pm}_{\Delta}$, and Mach numbers $\mathcal{M}_{\Delta} \in \{0.5, 1, 2\}$, combined with analytical models accounting for resistive losses and viscous layer broadening $\partial_{t}U=\nu\rho_{0}^{-1}\partial_{x}(\rho_{0}\partial_{x}U)$.
assumptions: Compressible Newtonian magnetohydrodynamics in a triply periodic domain with initial planar shear layer and density stratification.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “KHI-driven dynamo is not a turbulence dynamo, in that the kinematic growth rates become independent of $\mathrm{Re}$.”
III Results: “We will next show that the $\mathrm{Re}_{\Delta}^{1/3}$ growth-rate scaling sets the subsequent dynamo onset time.”
IV Discussion: “This suggests that global merger simulations are time-resolving the wrong KHI-driven dynamo stage”
Equations and numerical methods.: “We solve the compressible, Newtonian magnetohydrodynamics equations in the triply periodic domain $[-L/2,L/2]^{3}”
Induction and geometry.: “amplification therefore requires motions beyond the original shear, initially seeded by the RTI”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that the KHI-driven dynamo departs from standard small-scale turbulent dynamo theory (where $\gamma_E \propto \mathrm{Re}^{1/2}$), establishing that secondary RTI sets an asymptotic, $\mathrm{Re}$-independent growth rate $\gamma_E t_\Delta \approx 0.02$ and revealing that current global merger simulations have misidentified the physical dynamo stage.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates the nonlinear interaction of ultra-strong electromagnetic waves with dense pair plasma, discovering that wave depletion is dominated by surfing acceleration in self-generated longitudinal channel fields rather than plasma expulsion, directly revising wave-damping paradigms for fast radio bursts (FRBs).
analysis.result: Strong linearly polarized electromagnetic waves with $a_0 = |e|E_0/(mc\omega_0) = 50$ clear an evacuated channel in cold pair plasma ($n_0 = 10 n_{\rm cr}$) with a relativistic front velocity $\beta_b = v_b/c = 1/(1+\sqrt{\psi}) \approx 0.83\text{--}0.89$, where $\psi = 4n_0/(a_0^2 n_{\rm cr})$. Wave depletion is heavily dominated by longitudinal field acceleration ($W_x \gg W_y$) rather than transverse or piston-like clearing, transferring $\approx 85\%$ of pulse energy into pair kinetic energy. Particles phase-lock and 'surf' along the channel walls over $\Delta t \approx 50\tau$ in slightly superluminal fields ($v_* > c$, $\delta u = (v_*-c)/c \approx 8\times 10^{-3}$), acquiring maximum normalized energies scaling as $\Delta\tilde{\varepsilon} \equiv \Delta\varepsilon/(a_0 mc^2) \approx \frac{\pi}{\delta u}\frac{E_*}{E_0}\frac{\lambda_*}{\lambda_0} \approx 12$.
analysis.problem: Understanding the energy loss rate, channel formation dynamics, and particle acceleration mechanisms when a high-amplitude electromagnetic wave propagates through an overdense pair plasma, specifically addressing whether channel evacuation suppresses or enhances pulse damping in high-energy transient contexts like FRBs.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional particle-in-cell (3D PIC) simulations using a speed-of-light moving window framework, complemented by analytical 1D momentum-flux balance at relativistic reflection fronts, electric-field work decomposition $W_\alpha(t) = \int_0^t q E_\alpha v_\alpha dt'$, and electromagnetic waveguide models (straight mode condition $\nabla \cdot \bm{E} \approx 0$ and converging wall reflections).
assumptions: The plasma is composed of an unmagnetized, cold, uniform electron-positron ($e^\pm$) pair plasma without ambient background magnetic fields ($B_{\rm bg} = 0$).
limits: The current simulations omit the ultrastrong background magnetic field ($B_{\rm bg}$, where magnetization $\sigma \gg 1$) typical of the inner magnetar magnetospheres relevant to some FRB models.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “We find that the wave loses substantially more energy than required to clear the channel and show that this excess depletion is caused by particle acceleration in the longitudinal electric field inside the self-generated channel.”

II Self-consistent channel formation: “In an electron-ion plasma, the charge-separation electric field created during the expulsion of electrons would cause a channel in electron density to refill after the wave passes. No such field is generated in our simulation because”

V Particle acceleration inside the channel: “The histogram reveals that the highest-energy electrons have $W_{x}\gg W_{y}$. This means that the work performed by the longitudinal electric field is the dominant contribution to the energy gain of these particles.”

V Particle acceleration inside the channel: “The figure confirms the surfing picture suggested by the current-field alignment: the tracked electron remains in the accelerating phase of the longitudinal electric field, $E_{x}<0$, for $\Delta t\approx 50\tau$ while gaining energy.”

VI Estimate for energy gain from the longitudinal field: “The channel effectively serves as a waveguide. We first consider the simpler case of a straight waveguide. We label the longitudinal electric field and the relative degree of superluminality in this straight-waveguide approximation”
VII Summary and discussion: “Our results raise the possibility that filamentation can instead increase the damping rate by enabling fast particle heating near the walls of the channel.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that self-consistent channel clearing by strong EM waves in pair plasma produces sustained, phase-matched longitudinal electric fields $E_x$ that accelerate positrons and electrons in opposite spatial phases along the walls ($j_x E_x > 0$), turning channel-forming filamentation into an active dissipation channel that can increase rather than decrease FRB damping rates.

analysis.reason: This work presents multi-epoch optical polarimetric monitoring of the Be/X-ray pulsar binary LS V +44 17 following its 2023 giant outburst, placing geometric constraints on the circumstellar decretion disk and its alignment with the neutron star accretion flow.
analysis.result: After correcting for an interstellar polarization of $P_{\rm IS} \approx 2.5\% - 2.9\%$, the intrinsic optical polarization degree is $P \approx 0.5\% - 1.7\%$, decreasing with wavelength from the $B$ band to the $R$ band (e.g., in Epoch 1, $P_B = 1.747\% \pm 0.004\%$ down to $P_R = 0.945\% \pm 0.001\%$). The intrinsic polarization angle lies in the range $\mathrm{PA} \approx 59^\circ - 68^\circ$, aligning closely with the pulse-independent X-ray polarization angle ($\approx 70^\circ$).
analysis.reading_entry: 4.2 Origin of the intrinsic optical polarization from LS V +44 17
analysis.problem: Identifying whether the variable optical linear polarization in the Be/X-ray pulsar LS V +44 17 originates from XRP magnetospheric synchrotron emission, X-ray reprocessing/irradiation, or electron scattering within a warped and precessing Be companion decretion disk.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch polarimetric observations were conducted in the $B$, $V$, and $R$ bands using DIPol-2 and DIPol-UF polarimeters. Normalized Stokes parameters $q$ and $u$ were measured to derive polarization degree $P=\sqrt{q^2+u^2}$ and position angle $\theta=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{atan2}(u,q)$. Interstellar polarization was determined and subtracted using parallax-matched ($\pi \approx 0.38 \pm 0.02\,\mathrm{mas}$) field stars, and temporal variability was evaluated using the multivariate Hotelling $T^2$ test.
assumptions: The neutron star dipolar magnetic field falls off as $B_{\rm mag} \propto r^{-3}$.
citation_leads: 2 Data: “Optical polarimetric data of LS V +44 17 were obtained using two copies of DIPol-2 polarimeters”

3.2 Interstellar polarization: “In all three filters, the Stokes parameters of the target cluster in a region separate from region occupied by the field stars on the $q$–$u$ plane, indicating that LS V +44 17 has a significantly distinguished intrinsic polarization.”

4.2.2 Synchrotron emission from the XRP: “As the dipole magnetic field strength falls $B_{\rm mag}\propto 1/r^{3}$ with distance from the XRP, and assuming that the optical emission is produced from a region where the magnetic field is $10^{5}$ G”

analysis.reason: The paper introduces APOLLO-Timing, an annealed phase-orbit lattice method designed to achieve coherent phase connection for sparsely observed binary pulsars without initial orbital ephemerides, and demonstrates it on FAST observations of PSR J1912-1215.
analysis.result: Using APOLLO-Timing on FAST data spanning $1438.07\,\mathrm{d}$, the authors obtained a fully phase-connected timing solution for PSR J1912$-$1215 with pulse frequency $\nu = 189.047239445402(8)\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ ($P \approx 5.29\,\mathrm{ms}$), $\dot{\nu} = -3.024(2)\times 10^{-16}\,\mathrm{s^{-2}}$, orbital period $P_b = 17.526125680(7)\,\mathrm{d}$, projected semi-major axis $x = 23.4476454(6)\,\mathrm{lt\text{-}s}$, $\mathrm{DM} = 39.495(1)\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, characteristic age $\tau_c = 9.90\times 10^9\,\mathrm{yr}$, and companion mass $m_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 0.67\,M_{\odot}$ (assuming $m_{\mathrm{p}}=1.4\,M_{\odot}$ and $i=60^{\circ}$).
analysis.problem: Large gaps between sparse follow-up observations of newly discovered binary pulsars prevent unambiguous determination of integer pulse counts and orbital parameters across observing sessions.
analysis.method: The framework models intra-session phase evolution via projection matrices $\mathbf{P}_s = \mathbf{I}_s - \mathbf{1}_s(\mathbf{1}_s^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{W}_s\mathbf{1}_s)^{-1}\mathbf{1}_s^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{W}_s$, employs an annealed noise covariance matrix $\mathbf{V}_{\tau}=\mathbf{V}+\tau^{2}(\mathbf{I}_{S-1}+\mathbf{1}_{S-1}\mathbf{1}_{S-1}^{\mathsf{T}})$ to progressively reduce artificial phase uncertainty from $\tau_0$ to $\tau=0$, and performs full-timing weighted least-squares fits with pulse-number tracking in PINT.
assumptions: Pulse count errors across gaps shift all pulse numbers within an observing session by a single integer offset without distorting relative intra-session phase differences
citation_leads: APOLLO-Timing: Annealed Phase–Orbit Lattice Linking across Observations for Binary Pulsar Timing: “We present APOLLO-Timing, a Bayesian phase–orbit lattice method that fits timing parameters together with integer pulse offsets between observing sessions.”

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the effects of temperature-dependent Wolf-Rayet stellar winds on progenitor mass loss and final remnant masses, providing crucial constraints on the circumstellar medium density profiles and progenitor cores of stripped-envelope supernovae and stellar-mass black holes.
analysis.result: Incorporating temperature-dependent Wolf-Rayet winds according to $\log_{10}(\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S23}}) = \log_{10}(\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S20}}) - 6\log_{10}(T_{\mathrm{eff,crit}}/141\,\mathrm{kK})$ leads to an effective scaling $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S23}} \propto T_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-6}$. At solar metallicity ($Z=0.014$), the final stellar mass saturates at $M_{\mathrm{final}} \approx 15\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} \ge 60\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, aligning well with dynamically measured black hole masses in Cygnus X-1 ($12\text{--}18\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and LMC binaries. Binary stripping lowers the threshold for WR formation to $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} \approx 23\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ at $Z=0.00224$.
analysis.problem: Standard Wolf-Rayet stellar evolution models suffer from the 'WR radius problem' and routinely omit the strong temperature dependence of optically thick wind mass loss, leading to discrepancies with modern hydrodynamically consistent atmosphere models.
analysis.method: MESA (v15140) stellar evolution models of non-rotating single and binary stars ($P_{\mathrm{i}} = 5, 30\,\mathrm{d}$; $q=0.5, 0.8$) across metallicities $Z \in \{0.014, 0.0056, 0.00224\}$ and initial masses $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} = 16\text{--}135\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, evolved from ZAMS through core carbon burning using a multi-regime wind prescription parameterized by Eddington factor $\Gamma_{\mathrm{e}} = 10^{-4.51} q_{\mathrm{ion}} \frac{L/\mathrm{L}_{\odot}}{M/\mathrm{M}_{\odot}}$ and transformed radius $R_{\mathrm{t}}$.
assumptions: Stellar evolution tracked from ZAMS until the cessation of core carbon burning
citation_leads: The formation and evolution of Wolf–Rayet stars with temperature-dependent winds: “Recent hydrodynamically consistent atmosphere calculations predict WR mass-loss rates that depend strongly on the temperature”
2 Numerical method: “The stars are evolved from the ZAMS until the end of core carbon burning.”
3 Stellar evolution and WR formation: “the cWR mass-loss rate depends steeply on temperature, approximately as $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S23}}\propto T_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-6}$”
5 Final masses: “the final mass saturates at about $15\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}}\geq 60\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$.”

analysis.reason: This paper focuses on galactic-scale 3D MHD simulations of cosmic-ray transport and spallation to explain the early Solar System 10Be/9Be abundance ratio recorded in meteorites. It does not address FRBs, PRS environments, relativistic jets, core-collapse supernova central engines, or high-energy transient phenomena.
analysis.result: The Galactic distribution of $^{10}\mathrm{Be}$ is overwhelmingly dominated by Galactic cosmic ray (GCR) spallation on ISM gas rather than direct SNR spallation (which contributes $\lesssim 10\%$ by volume and $\lesssim 1\%$ by gas mass). In newly formed stars (formed within 5 Myr), the inherited $^{10}\mathrm{Be}/^{9}\mathrm{Be}$ ratio is enhanced by a factor of $\sim 5$ compared to volume-weighted ISM gas due to spatial correlation with SN injection sites, yielding values consistent with the early Solar System meteoritic value $^{10}\mathrm{Be}/^{9}\mathrm{Be} \approx 7\times 10^{-4}$ under an enhanced star formation rate factor $\Psi = 2.0$ at the epoch of Solar System formation without requiring local irradiation.
analysis.problem: Whether the early Solar System abundance of short-lived radionuclide $^{10}\mathrm{Be}$ ($t_{1/2} = 1.387\ \mathrm{Myr}$), measured in CAIs to be $^{10}\mathrm{Be}/^{9}\mathrm{Be} \approx 7\times 10^{-4}$, originated from local irradiation by protosolar energetic particles or can be explained by inheritance from the parent molecular cloud permeated by Galactic cosmic rays.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional hydrodynamic AMR simulations using Enzo coupled with the Grackle cooling library and two-fluid cosmic ray transport with diffusion coefficient $\kappa_{\rm CR} = (1\text{--}10) \times 10^{28}\ \mathrm{cm}^2\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ on an AGORA-like isolated MW disc, tracking $^{10}\mathrm{Be}$ advection, radioactive decay, GCR spallation $P_{^{10}\mathrm{Be}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = P_{^{10}\mathrm{Be,Local}}[\epsilon_{\rm CR}(\boldsymbol{x})/\epsilon_{\rm CR,Local}]$, and SNR production scaled by $Q_{^{10}\mathrm{Be}} \simeq C_{^{10}\mathrm{Be}} n_{\rm H}$.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “Analyses of primitive inclusions in meteorites, such as calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions (CAIs) and chondrules, have revealed that the early Solar System was enriched in more than ten short-lived radionuclides”

II.5.1 GCR production of 10Be: “The production rate of 10Be per hydrogen atom, $P_{{}^{10}\mathrm{Be}}$ [atoms yr-1 H-1], is calculated by integrating the product of the differential GCR intensity and the spallation cross section over particle energy”

IV.1 Initial 10Be/9Be ratio and the Solar birth environment: “This suggests that inheritance of GCR-produced 10Be from the parent molecular cloud can account for the early Solar System’s 10Be/9Be without invoking a late injection or local irradiation.”

analysis.reason: This work extends the open-source 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer code SKIRT to compute photon arrival time lags, providing a self-consistent tool for high-energy reverberation mapping and echo studies in complex compact object environments.
analysis.result: The code successfully recovers time lag distributions in arbitrary 3D geometries. In optically thick media, late-time transmission lags decay exponentially as $F_{\mathrm{t}}(t) \propto \exp(-\tau_{\mathrm{es}} c \,\delta t / D)$, with the mean time lag $\langle\delta t\rangle$ converging to the skin-depth lag $\delta t_{0.5} \equiv 2 d_{0.5}/c$. Owing to $\sigma_{\mathrm{PA}}(E) \propto E^{-3}$, neutral Fe K$\alpha$ fluorescence ($6.38\text{--}6.42\ \mathrm{keV}$, threshold $7.112\ \mathrm{keV}$) penetrates deeper and exhibits longer arrival delays than the continuum, producing a peak reverberation lag $\tau_{\mathrm{peak}} \approx 2.39 \times 10^6\ \mathrm{s}$ ($\approx 28\ \mathrm{d}$) for an AGN torus model around a $M_\bullet = 10^7 M_\odot$ black hole. Simulation efficiency is characterized by $\mathrm{FOM} \equiv 1 / (R^2 T)$ with convergence criteria $R < 0.1$ and $\mathrm{VOV} < 0.1$.
analysis.reading_entry: Photon arrival time lags in 3D radiative transfer with SKIRT
analysis.problem: Self-consistently calculating energy-dependent photon arrival time lags, reverberation transfer functions, and Compton echo profiles across complex, non-spherical 3D circumstellar and circumnuclear media around high-energy compact objects.
analysis.method: Implemented path-length accumulation in 3D Monte Carlo code SKIRT: photon packets track cumulative spatial path $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq \mathcal{D} + |\mathbf{r}_{i} - \mathbf{r}_{i-1}|$, with peel-off emission corrected for coordinate origin projection $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq -\mathbf{\hat{n}}_{\mathrm{obs}}\cdot\mathbf{r}_0$ and exit lag $\delta t = (\mathcal{D} - \mathbf{\hat{n}}_{\mathrm{obs}} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{i})/c$. Handled Klein-Nishina electron scattering and photoelectric absorption with Fe K$\alpha$ fluorescence, and convolved transfer functions with damped random walk (DRW) light curves to compute cross-correlation functions (CCF).

analysis.reason: This paper evaluates the impact of updated Bayesian carbon-fusion rates and carbon-helium rates on white-dwarf heating and the pair-instability black-hole mass boundary, providing crucial nuclear inputs for compact object formation and supernova progenitor modeling.
analysis.result: For accreting carbon-oxygen white dwarfs at $\dot{M} = 10^{-7}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the Bayesian median rate delays the thermal equilibrium $L_{\rm nuc} = L_{\nu} + L_{\gamma}$, yielding a central temperature $\sim 2.57\%$ higher and central density $18.9\%$ higher than standard CF88 rates. In $20\,M_{\odot}$ stars at core carbon exhaustion, the updated rates and branching increase ${}^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$ retained mass by $+10.78\%$ and decrease ${}^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ by $-28.70\%$. Across low metallicities ($Z = 10^{-5}$), constraining the astrophysical factor to $S_{\rm tot}(300\,\mathrm{keV}) = 118 \pm 17\,\mathrm{keV\,b}$ sets the maximum black-hole mass at the lower edge of the pair-instability gap to $61.48 \lesssim M_{\rm BH,max}/M_{\odot} \lesssim 77.35$, where $M_{\rm BH} \simeq M_{\rm initial} - M_{\rm wind} - M_{\rm PPISN} - \Delta M_{\rm collapse}$.

analysis.reason: This work explores black hole spin evolution and equilibrium spin limits using GRMHD simulations across various magnetic field geometries, providing key constraints on central engine efficiency and relativistic jet launching.
analysis.result: Using 2D GRMHD simulations across $\chi \in [0, 0.99]$, the equilibrium spin $\chi_{\rm eq}$ (where $\langle\dot{\chi}\rangle = 0$ for $\dot{\chi} = \dot{J}_h/M^2 - 2\chi\dot{M}_h/M$) is shown to depend sensitively on magnetic topology: a fiducial model ($\beta_{\max} = 100$) reaches $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.88$, multiple loops give $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.87$, strong magnetic fields ($\beta_{\max} = 10$) rapidly disrupt the torus shifting turnover to $\chi \in [0.37, 0.71]$, while radially modulated magnetic flux permits near-extremal spin $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.98$. The physical spin evolution rate scales as $\dot{\chi}^{\rm phys} \approx 2\times 10^{-8} f_{\rm Edd}\dot{\chi}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, implying evolution timescales $>10^{13}\,{\rm yr}$ for Sgr A* under its current low accretion rate.
analysis.reading_entry: How Fast do Black Holes Spin?
analysis.problem: How magnetic stresses across the ISCO and jet angular momentum extraction modify the equilibrium spin $\chi_{\rm eq}$ and spin evolution of accreting black holes relative to the standard Novikov-Thorne thin-disk radiative capture limit ($\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.998$).
analysis.method: Axisymmetric GRMHD simulations using BHAC in fixed Kerr spacetime with Fishbone-Moncrief equilibrium tori (adiabatic index $\Gamma = 4/3$, specific angular momentum $\ell = u_\phi/u_t$, and effective potential $W(r,\theta)$), seeding poloidal magnetic fields via vector potential $A_\phi(r,\theta) = [\rho(r,\theta) - \rho_{\rm cut}]_+ f_\theta(\theta) f_r(r)$ normalized by $\beta_{\max} = p_{\max}/(b_{\max}^2/2)$, and extracting horizon mass flux $\dot{M}_h$ and angular momentum flux $\dot{J}_h$ to measure $\dot{\chi} = \dot{J}_h/M^2 - 2\chi\dot{M}_h/M$.

analysis.reason: The paper demonstrates that a first-order hadron-quark phase transition can dynamically collapse neutron stars into black holes with masses below the maximum stable hybrid star limit via Type-I critical phenomena, naturally triggering blitzar-like magnetic field ejection and potential fast radio bursts (FRBs).
analysis.result: Dynamic collapse of a hadronic neutron star triggered by deconfinement can occur despite the existence of radially stable hybrid star configurations with identical baryon mass $M_B$, lowering the black hole formation threshold by $\Delta M_B \approx 0.12\,M_\odot$ below the static threshold. The transition behaves as a Type-I critical collapse governed by $T_0 = C - \lambda^{-1} \ln |p - p^*|$, where the measured scaling slope $\lambda^{-1} = 74 \pm 3\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ (or $15.1 \pm 0.4 \pm 0.3\,M_\odot$ in geometric units) matches the inverse growth rate of the unstable radial fundamental mode $1/|\omega_0| = 71.9\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ ($14.60\,M_\odot$). Horizon formation within $0.3$--$1.3\,\mathrm{ms}$ sheds the magnetosphere, potentially powering an FRB-like radio burst.

analysis.method: General relativistic hydrodynamic simulations in spherical symmetry using an extended version of GR1D under polar slicing and radial gauge, adopting piecewise-polytropic equations of state with thermal contributions $P = P_{\mathrm{cold}} + (\Gamma_{\mathrm{th}} - 1)\rho[\epsilon - \epsilon_{\mathrm{cold}}]$ (with $\Gamma_{\mathrm{th}} = 1.75$) and bisection searching for the critical initial density $\rho_{c,0}$ or inward velocity perturbation $V(r) = (v_0/2)(x^3 - 3x)$. Radial instability modes $|\omega| = \sqrt{-\omega^2}$ are verified via a 1D finite-element perturbation solver.

analysis.reason: This work quantitatively computes one-loop QED dispersion relations and time delays for photons traversing magnetized vacuum and degenerate plasma in neutron star magnetospheres, revealing that vacuum birefringence induces delays of $\sim 10-10^3\ \mathrm{ns}$ while plasma medium effects can reach milliseconds in the X-ray band.
analysis.result: In the weak-field limit ($eB \ll m_e^2$), the vacuum phase velocities scale as $v_V^{\mathrm{WF},(1,2)} \approx 1 - \frac{\alpha}{90\pi}\left(\frac{B}{B_c}\right)^2$ and $v_V^{\mathrm{WF},(3)} \approx 1 - \frac{\alpha}{30\pi}\left(\frac{B}{B_c}\right)^2$, whereas in the strong-field limit ($eB \gg m_e^2$), mode 3 saturates to $v_V^{\mathrm{SF},(3)} \approx 1 - \frac{\alpha}{3\pi}$ independent of $B$ due to lowest Landau level dominance. For magnetar magnetospheres, the integrated propagation delay in Schwarzschild spacetime, $\Delta\tau = \int_{r_0}^{r_0+L} dr \left(\frac{1}{v_p} - 1\right) \left(1 - \frac{2M}{r}\right)^{-1}$, yields nanosecond-to-microsecond delays for pure vacuum QED ($\,\Delta\tau_V \sim 10-10^3\ \mathrm{ns}\,$, reducing by a factor of 5 when transitioning from toroidal to dipole decay), whereas the degenerate electron-positron medium contribution reaches the millisecond scale ($\Delta\tau_M \sim 10^{-1}-10^2\ \mathrm{ms}$) at X-ray frequencies $\hbar\omega \sim 1-100\ \mathrm{keV}$.

analysis.problem: Accreting-only symbiotic stars in long quiescent phases ($L_{\rm acc} \lesssim 3\,L_\odot$) dominate the Galactic symbiotic population but have remained largely undetected due to their weak Balmer emission and lack of strong nuclear burning.

analysis.reason: The paper develops and benchmarks an autonomous multi-agent pipeline with strict provenance validation for high-energy astrophysics data reduction, demonstrating high fidelity on IXPE polarimetric observations of black hole X-ray binaries.
analysis.result: The pipeline reproduced published IXPE polarimetric measurements of Cyg X-1 with all 14 quantities agreeing within $3\sigma$ (polarization angle deviation $<0.5\sigma$; energy dependence slope in ${\rm PD}(E)=A+B\,(E/\mathrm{keV}-1)$ within $0.24\sigma$, while polarization degrees were offset by $0.2$--$2.4\sigma$). In a sample of 29 IXPE observations across six BHXRBs, 2–8 keV polarization degree correlated strongly with spectral hardness ${\rm HR}=(H-S)/(H+S)$ (Spearman $\rho=0.947, p=2.5\times 10^{-12}$), and a candidate Stokes $q$–$u$ time lag peak was recovered in Cyg X-3 with lag interval $[-100.94, -57.68]\text{ ks}$ ($p<0.01$).
analysis.problem: Large language model (LLM) agents deployed for astronomical data processing frequently suffer from data fabrication, silent execution failures, and circumvented code validation checks when handling complex high-energy observational pipelines.
analysis.method: A multi-agent architecture built on LangGraph orchestrating HEASoft, XSPEC, and ixpeobssim within containerized sandboxes, utilizing automated deterministic/anti-fabrication gates, cross-model code review (co-lead), two-repository sandbox separation, and report provenance validators requiring traceability to tool execution logs or literature.
limits: Strict provenance enforcement certifies that reported numbers trace to execution logs or literature citations, but does not guarantee physical validity of underlying models

analysis.reason: The paper demonstrates that 3D radiative relativistic magnetic reconnection in black hole coronae can simultaneously self-regulate pair loading, produce seed photons, and account for the observed MeV tail in X-ray binaries like Cygnus X-1.
analysis.result: Free particles escaping flux ropes in 3D relativistic reconnection accelerate to the synchrotron burnoff limit ($\sim 16\,\mathrm{MeV}$), yielding a ratio of synchrotron to inverse Compton power $\xi \sim 0.25\text{--}0.5$ (up to $0.5\text{--}0.9$ with full cooling). In a corona of size $R \sim 2 \times 10^6 \sqrt{1+\xi}\,\mathrm{cm}$ and magnetic field $B \sim 10^8\,\mathrm{G}$, high-energy $\gamma$-rays experience $\gamma\gamma$ absorption with optical depth $\tau_{\gamma\gamma} \simeq 40 (\varepsilon_1 / 100\,\mathrm{keV})^{-0.7} (\varepsilon_\gamma / m_e c^2)^{0.3}$ for $\varepsilon_\gamma \gg (m_e c^2)^2/\varepsilon_1 \simeq 2.6\,\mathrm{MeV}$. analysis.problem: Long-period binary systems ($P \gtrsim 10\,\mathrm{yr}$) lack closed Keplerian orbital solutions within the 34-month Gaia DR3 baseline, and astrometric acceleration alone suffers from severe parameter degeneracies when identifying massive compact object companions.

assumptions: The luminous primary star orbits an unseen point-mass companion under Newtonian two-body Keplerian gravity.

analysis.result: The neural operator accelerates rotating relativistic star solutions by a factor of $\sim 10^3\times$ (reducing computation time from $45\,\mathrm{s}$ with traditional RNS solvers to $35\,\mathrm{ms}$, a $1283\times$ speed-up) while maintaining high fidelity, with stellar mass errors $|\Delta M| \sim 0.14\%$ and equatorial radius errors $|\Delta R| \sim 0.03\%$, enabling rigorous Bayesian MCMC EoS inference over rotating pulsar populations like PSR J0952$-$0607 ($M=2.35\pm 0.17\,M_{\odot}$, $\nu=707.3\,\mathrm{Hz}$).

analysis.problem: Traditional numerical solvers for rapidly rotating relativistic stars (e.g. iterative Green's function relaxation methods) are computationally prohibitive for large-scale Bayesian EoS parameter inference and population synthesis, whereas adopting non-rotating TOV models or low-order perturbative approximations introduces severe systematic biases.

analysis.reason: This work uncovers the physical chronology of the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (KHI) kinematic dynamo in binary neutron star mergers, showing that the dynamo is not standard turbulence-driven because asymptotic growth rates become independent of $\mathrm{Re}$, mediated instead by secondary Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI).
analysis.result: The KHI dynamo operates across three stages: Stage 1 shear winding produces a flat spectrum $E_{\rm mag}(k) \propto k^{0}$ with energy scaling $E_{\rm wound,peak}/E_{\rm mag,0} \propto \mathrm{Pm}_{\Delta}^{2/3}$. Secondary centrifugal RTI then disrupts the vortices with growth rate $\gamma_{\rm RTI}^{\infty}t_{\Delta} = \frac{3}{4^{4/3}}[\frac{Ag_{\rm eff}\delta_{0}}{(\Delta U)^{2}}]^{2/3}\mathrm{Re}_{\Delta}^{1/3}$, imposing a dynamo onset delay $t_{\rm delay}/t_{\Delta} \propto \mathrm{Re}_{\Delta}^{-1/3}$. At high Reynolds numbers ($\,\mathrm{Re}_\Delta \ge 512$), the kinematic growth rate saturates to an $\mathrm{Re}$-independent value $\gamma_{E}t_{\Delta} \sim 0.02$ (yielding $\gamma_E \simeq 36\,\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ for BNS parameters) with a Kazantsev spectrum $E_{\rm mag}(k) \propto k^{3/2}$, directly amplifying mean vertical fields to $\overline{B}_{z} \sim 10^{14}\text{--}10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ at an unresolvable microscopic scale $\lambda_{\rm RTI}^{\infty} \approx 6\,\mathrm{cm}$.
analysis.problem: Global binary neutron star merger simulations observe magnetic field amplification at shear interfaces but suffer from numerical dissipation; whether the amplification is a standard small-scale turbulent dynamo with growth rate $\gamma_E \propto \mathrm{Re}^{1/2}$ or driven by resolved shear winding remained controversial.
analysis.method: Direct numerical simulations of 3D compressible Newtonian viscous-resistive MHD using AthenaK on triply periodic domains ($1152^3\text{--}2304^3$ grid cells) covering $64 \le \mathrm{Re}_{\Delta} \le 16384$, magnetic Prandtl numbers $\mathrm{Pm}_{\Delta}$, and Mach numbers $\mathcal{M}_{\Delta} \in \{0.5, 1, 2\}$, combined with analytical models accounting for resistive losses and viscous layer broadening $\partial_{t}U=\nu\rho_{0}^{-1}\partial_{x}(\rho_{0}\partial_{x}U)$.
assumptions: Compressible Newtonian magnetohydrodynamics in a triply periodic domain with initial planar shear layer and density stratification.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “KHI-driven dynamo is not a turbulence dynamo, in that the kinematic growth rates become independent of $\mathrm{Re}$.”
III Results: “We will next show that the $\mathrm{Re}_{\Delta}^{1/3}$ growth-rate scaling sets the subsequent dynamo onset time.”
IV Discussion: “This suggests that global merger simulations are time-resolving the wrong KHI-driven dynamo stage”
Equations and numerical methods.: “We solve the compressible, Newtonian magnetohydrodynamics equations in the triply periodic domain $[-L/2,L/2]^{3}”
Induction and geometry.: “amplification therefore requires motions beyond the original shear, initially seeded by the RTI”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that the KHI-driven dynamo departs from standard small-scale turbulent dynamo theory (where $\gamma_E \propto \mathrm{Re}^{1/2}$), establishing that secondary RTI sets an asymptotic, $\mathrm{Re}$-independent growth rate $\gamma_E t_\Delta \approx 0.02$ and revealing that current global merger simulations have misidentified the physical dynamo stage.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates the nonlinear interaction of ultra-strong electromagnetic waves with dense pair plasma, discovering that wave depletion is dominated by surfing acceleration in self-generated longitudinal channel fields rather than plasma expulsion, directly revising wave-damping paradigms for fast radio bursts (FRBs).
analysis.result: Strong linearly polarized electromagnetic waves with $a_0 = |e|E_0/(mc\omega_0) = 50$ clear an evacuated channel in cold pair plasma ($n_0 = 10 n_{\rm cr}$) with a relativistic front velocity $\beta_b = v_b/c = 1/(1+\sqrt{\psi}) \approx 0.83\text{--}0.89$, where $\psi = 4n_0/(a_0^2 n_{\rm cr})$. Wave depletion is heavily dominated by longitudinal field acceleration ($W_x \gg W_y$) rather than transverse or piston-like clearing, transferring $\approx 85\%$ of pulse energy into pair kinetic energy. Particles phase-lock and 'surf' along the channel walls over $\Delta t \approx 50\tau$ in slightly superluminal fields ($v_* > c$, $\delta u = (v_*-c)/c \approx 8\times 10^{-3}$), acquiring maximum normalized energies scaling as $\Delta\tilde{\varepsilon} \equiv \Delta\varepsilon/(a_0 mc^2) \approx \frac{\pi}{\delta u}\frac{E_*}{E_0}\frac{\lambda_*}{\lambda_0} \approx 12$.
analysis.problem: Understanding the energy loss rate, channel formation dynamics, and particle acceleration mechanisms when a high-amplitude electromagnetic wave propagates through an overdense pair plasma, specifically addressing whether channel evacuation suppresses or enhances pulse damping in high-energy transient contexts like FRBs.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional particle-in-cell (3D PIC) simulations using a speed-of-light moving window framework, complemented by analytical 1D momentum-flux balance at relativistic reflection fronts, electric-field work decomposition $W_\alpha(t) = \int_0^t q E_\alpha v_\alpha dt'$, and electromagnetic waveguide models (straight mode condition $\nabla \cdot \bm{E} \approx 0$ and converging wall reflections).
assumptions: The plasma is composed of an unmagnetized, cold, uniform electron-positron ($e^\pm$) pair plasma without ambient background magnetic fields ($B_{\rm bg} = 0$).
limits: The current simulations omit the ultrastrong background magnetic field ($B_{\rm bg}$, where magnetization $\sigma \gg 1$) typical of the inner magnetar magnetospheres relevant to some FRB models.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “We find that the wave loses substantially more energy than required to clear the channel and show that this excess depletion is caused by particle acceleration in the longitudinal electric field inside the self-generated channel.”

II Self-consistent channel formation: “In an electron-ion plasma, the charge-separation electric field created during the expulsion of electrons would cause a channel in electron density to refill after the wave passes. No such field is generated in our simulation because”

V Particle acceleration inside the channel: “The histogram reveals that the highest-energy electrons have $W_{x}\gg W_{y}$. This means that the work performed by the longitudinal electric field is the dominant contribution to the energy gain of these particles.”

V Particle acceleration inside the channel: “The figure confirms the surfing picture suggested by the current-field alignment: the tracked electron remains in the accelerating phase of the longitudinal electric field, $E_{x}<0$, for $\Delta t\approx 50\tau$ while gaining energy.”

VI Estimate for energy gain from the longitudinal field: “The channel effectively serves as a waveguide. We first consider the simpler case of a straight waveguide. We label the longitudinal electric field and the relative degree of superluminality in this straight-waveguide approximation”
VII Summary and discussion: “Our results raise the possibility that filamentation can instead increase the damping rate by enabling fast particle heating near the walls of the channel.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that self-consistent channel clearing by strong EM waves in pair plasma produces sustained, phase-matched longitudinal electric fields $E_x$ that accelerate positrons and electrons in opposite spatial phases along the walls ($j_x E_x > 0$), turning channel-forming filamentation into an active dissipation channel that can increase rather than decrease FRB damping rates.

figures.label: Fig. 9

analysis.reason: This work presents multi-epoch optical polarimetric monitoring of the Be/X-ray pulsar binary LS V +44 17 following its 2023 giant outburst, placing geometric constraints on the circumstellar decretion disk and its alignment with the neutron star accretion flow.
analysis.result: After correcting for an interstellar polarization of $P_{\rm IS} \approx 2.5\% - 2.9\%$, the intrinsic optical polarization degree is $P \approx 0.5\% - 1.7\%$, decreasing with wavelength from the $B$ band to the $R$ band (e.g., in Epoch 1, $P_B = 1.747\% \pm 0.004\%$ down to $P_R = 0.945\% \pm 0.001\%$). The intrinsic polarization angle lies in the range $\mathrm{PA} \approx 59^\circ - 68^\circ$, aligning closely with the pulse-independent X-ray polarization angle ($\approx 70^\circ$).
analysis.reading_entry: 4.2 Origin of the intrinsic optical polarization from LS V +44 17
analysis.problem: Identifying whether the variable optical linear polarization in the Be/X-ray pulsar LS V +44 17 originates from XRP magnetospheric synchrotron emission, X-ray reprocessing/irradiation, or electron scattering within a warped and precessing Be companion decretion disk.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch polarimetric observations were conducted in the $B$, $V$, and $R$ bands using DIPol-2 and DIPol-UF polarimeters. Normalized Stokes parameters $q$ and $u$ were measured to derive polarization degree $P=\sqrt{q^2+u^2}$ and position angle $\theta=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{atan2}(u,q)$. Interstellar polarization was determined and subtracted using parallax-matched ($\pi \approx 0.38 \pm 0.02\,\mathrm{mas}$) field stars, and temporal variability was evaluated using the multivariate Hotelling $T^2$ test.
assumptions: The neutron star dipolar magnetic field falls off as $B_{\rm mag} \propto r^{-3}$.
citation_leads: 2 Data: “Optical polarimetric data of LS V +44 17 were obtained using two copies of DIPol-2 polarimeters”

3.2 Interstellar polarization: “In all three filters, the Stokes parameters of the target cluster in a region separate from region occupied by the field stars on the $q$–$u$ plane, indicating that LS V +44 17 has a significantly distinguished intrinsic polarization.”

4.2.2 Synchrotron emission from the XRP: “As the dipole magnetic field strength falls $B_{\rm mag}\propto 1/r^{3}$ with distance from the XRP, and assuming that the optical emission is produced from a region where the magnetic field is $10^{5}$ G”
4.2.3 Be decretion disk: “The obtained intrinsic optical PA in the range of $59\degr$–$68\degr$ is in close agreement with the PA of the pulse-independent component of X-ray polarization”
analysis.research_progress: Rules out XRP magnetospheric synchrotron emission and direct X-ray illumination as the primary polarization drivers, establishing that electron scattering within a warped, precessing Be decretion disk explains the wavelength-dependent PA and the $\sim 1000\,\mathrm{d}$ long-term secular evolution.

analysis.reason: The paper provides experimental upper bounds from the Pierre Auger Observatory on diffuse ultrahigh-energy (UHE) sterile neutrinos ($0.3\text{--}200\,\mathrm{EeV}$) mixing with $\nu_\tau$, which directly connects to UHE neutrino propagation and high-energy astrophysical transient sources.
analysis.result: For an assumed $E^{-2}$ flux spectrum across $[0.3, 200]\,\mathrm{EeV}$ and mixing angle $\sin^2\theta_N \lesssim 10^{-1}$, the 90% C.L. upper bound on the diffuse sterile neutrino flux is $E^2\Phi_N \le 2\times 10^{-9}\sin^{-2}\theta_N\,\mathrm{GeV}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, with detection exposure dominated by Earth-skimming showers.
analysis.problem: Investigating whether ultrahigh-energy sterile neutrinos in the $m_N \sim 1\text{--}100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ range mixing with $\nu_\tau$ can penetrate Earth over long chord lengths and produce detectable tau-induced air showers at the Pierre Auger Observatory.
analysis.method: A $3+1$ neutrino framework is employed with effective mixing angle $\sin^2\theta_N = |U_{\tau 4}|^2$. Monte Carlo simulations model $N_1$ propagation through Earth (PREM model), tau lepton continuous energy loss $-\mathrm{d}E_\tau/\mathrm{d}x \simeq b(E_\tau)E_\tau$, and decay into air showers to evaluate exposure $\mathcal{E}_N(E; \theta_N)$ in Earth-skimming and upward-going channels.
assumptions: A minimal $3+1$ neutrino model where one sterile mass eigenstate $N_1$ mixes predominantly only with the $\nu_\tau$ flavor via $|U_{\tau 4}|^2 = \sin^2\theta_N$.
limits: Active-sterile mixing angle restricted to $\sin^2\theta_N \lesssim 10^{-1}$.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “In this work, we consider a $3+1$ framework in which one sterile state mixes appreciably only with the $\uptau$ flavor.”

analysis.reason: This white-paper/review highlights spatially-resolved IFU spectroscopy (specifically SHARP/VESPER) to resolve local progenitor environments (metallicity, SFH) of LGRBs, stripped-envelope Ic-BL SNe, and kilonovae up to high redshifts ($z \sim 3$). It is directly relevant to understanding GRB central engine launch conditions, metallicity thresholds for jet breakouts versus choked jets, and host interstellar medium kinematics.
analysis.result: Local gas-phase metallicity and ionization diagnostics can be determined at sub-galactic scales for high-$z$ transients, avoiding galaxy-integrated biases. For simulated SHARP/VESPER observations ($\Delta\lambda = [0.95-2.45]\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, $R \approx 3000$) of a young ($0.1\,\mathrm{Gyr}$) stellar population, the rest-frame [O II] $\lambda\lambda 3727, 3729\,\mathrm{\AA}$ doublet reaches $\mathrm{SNR} = 10$ in $< 1.5\,\mathrm{hours}$ (spatial resampling $7\times 7$). Neutral/cold gas absorption metallicities and ionized gas emission metallicities agree within $\pm 0.4\,\mathrm{dex}$.
analysis.reading_entry: 2.2 The Puzzle of Ic-BL SNe without GRBs
analysis.problem: Galaxy-integrated properties (e.g. global metallicity and stellar mass) fail to capture immediate progenitor birth conditions in star-forming galaxies with steep metallicity gradients and chemical inhomogeneities, obscuring whether a hard metallicity boundary dictates relativistic jet formation (LGRBs vs. Ic-BL SNe without GRBs) and missing large offsets of kilonovae in host outskirts.
analysis.method: Stellar Population Synthesis (SPS; STARLIGHT, Bruzual & Charlot templates) fitting to spatially resolved stellar continua and emission line diagnostics (BPT, [O II], [O III], $\mathrm{H}\alpha$), along with SHARP Exposure Time Calculator simulations (ETC v0.6) compared against ESO/MUSE and JWST/G140M spectroscopy.
assumptions: GRB-SN progenitors have short lifetimes (~10-30 Myr) and explode close to their birth H II regions.
limits: Simulations assume template-based stellar populations and specific spatial binning configurations with the SHARP ETC v0.6.

analysis.reason: The paper introduces APOLLO-Timing, an annealed phase-orbit lattice method designed to achieve coherent phase connection for sparsely observed binary pulsars without initial orbital ephemerides, and demonstrates it on FAST observations of PSR J1912-1215.
analysis.result: Using APOLLO-Timing on FAST data spanning $1438.07\,\mathrm{d}$, the authors obtained a fully phase-connected timing solution for PSR J1912$-$1215 with pulse frequency $\nu = 189.047239445402(8)\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ ($P \approx 5.29\,\mathrm{ms}$), $\dot{\nu} = -3.024(2)\times 10^{-16}\,\mathrm{s^{-2}}$, orbital period $P_b = 17.526125680(7)\,\mathrm{d}$, projected semi-major axis $x = 23.4476454(6)\,\mathrm{lt\text{-}s}$, $\mathrm{DM} = 39.495(1)\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, characteristic age $\tau_c = 9.90\times 10^9\,\mathrm{yr}$, and companion mass $m_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 0.67\,M_{\odot}$ (assuming $m_{\mathrm{p}}=1.4\,M_{\odot}$ and $i=60^{\circ}$).
analysis.problem: Large gaps between sparse follow-up observations of newly discovered binary pulsars prevent unambiguous determination of integer pulse counts and orbital parameters across observing sessions.
analysis.method: The framework models intra-session phase evolution via projection matrices $\mathbf{P}_s = \mathbf{I}_s - \mathbf{1}_s(\mathbf{1}_s^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{W}_s\mathbf{1}_s)^{-1}\mathbf{1}_s^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{W}_s$, employs an annealed noise covariance matrix $\mathbf{V}_{\tau}=\mathbf{V}+\tau^{2}(\mathbf{I}_{S-1}+\mathbf{1}_{S-1}\mathbf{1}_{S-1}^{\mathsf{T}})$ to progressively reduce artificial phase uncertainty from $\tau_0$ to $\tau=0$, and performs full-timing weighted least-squares fits with pulse-number tracking in PINT.
assumptions: Pulse count errors across gaps shift all pulse numbers within an observing session by a single integer offset without distorting relative intra-session phase differences
citation_leads: APOLLO-Timing: Annealed Phase–Orbit Lattice Linking across Observations for Binary Pulsar Timing: “We present APOLLO-Timing, a Bayesian phase–orbit lattice method that fits timing parameters together with integer pulse offsets between observing sessions.”
II.1 Phase Information within Observations: “A count error across a gap shifts every pulse number in a session by the same integer, leaving their differences unchanged.”
II.5 Fits with the Full Timing Model: “Starting from the $\tau=0$ parameters, PINT fits the full model by weighted least squares with pulse-number tracking enabled.”
analysis.research_progress: Provides an automated, computationally lightweight ($914\,\mathrm{s}$, $255\,\mathrm{MiB}$) algorithm to solve orbital ephemerides and pulse-phase linking across multi-year observational baselines without prior orbital seeds.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the effects of temperature-dependent Wolf-Rayet stellar winds on progenitor mass loss and final remnant masses, providing crucial constraints on the circumstellar medium density profiles and progenitor cores of stripped-envelope supernovae and stellar-mass black holes.
analysis.result: Incorporating temperature-dependent Wolf-Rayet winds according to $\log_{10}(\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S23}}) = \log_{10}(\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S20}}) - 6\log_{10}(T_{\mathrm{eff,crit}}/141\,\mathrm{kK})$ leads to an effective scaling $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S23}} \propto T_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-6}$. At solar metallicity ($Z=0.014$), the final stellar mass saturates at $M_{\mathrm{final}} \approx 15\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} \ge 60\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, aligning well with dynamically measured black hole masses in Cygnus X-1 ($12\text{--}18\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and LMC binaries. Binary stripping lowers the threshold for WR formation to $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} \approx 23\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ at $Z=0.00224$.
analysis.problem: Standard Wolf-Rayet stellar evolution models suffer from the 'WR radius problem' and routinely omit the strong temperature dependence of optically thick wind mass loss, leading to discrepancies with modern hydrodynamically consistent atmosphere models.
analysis.method: MESA (v15140) stellar evolution models of non-rotating single and binary stars ($P_{\mathrm{i}} = 5, 30\,\mathrm{d}$; $q=0.5, 0.8$) across metallicities $Z \in \{0.014, 0.0056, 0.00224\}$ and initial masses $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} = 16\text{--}135\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, evolved from ZAMS through core carbon burning using a multi-regime wind prescription parameterized by Eddington factor $\Gamma_{\mathrm{e}} = 10^{-4.51} q_{\mathrm{ion}} \frac{L/\mathrm{L}_{\odot}}{M/\mathrm{M}_{\odot}}$ and transformed radius $R_{\mathrm{t}}$.
assumptions: Stellar evolution tracked from ZAMS until the cessation of core carbon burning
citation_leads: The formation and evolution of Wolf–Rayet stars with temperature-dependent winds: “Recent hydrodynamically consistent atmosphere calculations predict WR mass-loss rates that depend strongly on the temperature”
2 Numerical method: “The stars are evolved from the ZAMS until the end of core carbon burning.”
3 Stellar evolution and WR formation: “the cWR mass-loss rate depends steeply on temperature, approximately as $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{S23}}\propto T_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-6}$”
5 Final masses: “the final mass saturates at about $15\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}}\geq 60\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$.”

analysis.result: Every year of the 2022--2026 conjunctions shows clear Faraday RM excursions, and scattering-corrected DM captures solar wind variations down to $\Delta\mathrm{DM}=(3.95\pm 0.20)\times 10^{-3}~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, with RM sign flips in 2023, 2024, and 2026 marking line-of-sight crossings of the heliospheric current sheet separating opposite magnetic polarities.

opening_brief.intro: Featured reading: "The kinematic Kelvin-Helmholtz instability-driven dynamo: implications for merging compact objects" and 12 other key developments.

focus_paper.title: The kinematic Kelvin-Helmholtz instability-driven dynamo: implications for merging compact objects

must_read.label: The kinematic Kelvin-Helmholtz instability-driven dynamo: implications for merging compact objects
must_read.text: The KHI dynamo operates across three stages: Stage 1 shear winding produces a flat spectrum $E_{\rm mag}(k) \propto k^{0}$ with energy scaling $E_{\rm wound,peak}/E_{\rm mag,0} \propto \mathrm{Pm}_{\Delta}^{2/3}$.

must_read.label: Longitudinal-field particle acceleration in channels generated by strong electromagnetic waves in pair plasma
must_read.text: Strong linearly polarized electromagnetic waves with $a_0 = |e|E_0/(mc\omega_0) = 50$ clear an evacuated channel in cold pair plasma ($n_0 = 10 n_{\rm cr}$) with a relativistic front velocity $\beta_b = v_b/c = 1/(1+\sqrt{\psi}) \approx 0.83\text{--}0.89$, where $\psi = 4n_0/(a_0^2 n_{\rm cr})$.

key_highlights.title: The M87 Black Hole Mass from JWST and Keck Stellar Kinematics Spanning 10 pc to 10 kpc
key_highlights.result: The triaxial orbit modeling determines the central black hole mass to be $M_{\mathrm{BH}} = (5.38 \pm 0.13 \pm 0.22) \times 10^{9}\,M_{\odot}$ (with the second uncertainty from the distance $D = 16.8 \pm 0.7\,\mathrm{Mpc}$), corresponding to an angular gravitational radius $\theta_g \equiv GM_{\mathrm{BH}}/(c^2 D) = 3.16 \pm 0.08\,\mu\mathrm{as}$.

key_highlights.title: ReveaLLAGN 2: Exploring the Nuclear Gas and Stellar Kinematics of Nearby LLAGNs with JWST/NIRSpec IFU
key_highlights.result: Across eight LLAGNs with $M_{\rm BH} \sim 10^{5.5-9.8}\,M_\odot$ and $\log(L_{\rm bol}/L_{\rm Edd}) \approx -6$ to $-2.7$, molecular gas ($\mathrm{H}_2$) is generally kinematically cooler and rotation-dominated compared to stars, but displays kinematic PA decoupling in M81, M94, NGC 1052, and NGC 5128.

key_highlights.title: Identifying Compact Object Candidates using Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations and Jerks
key_highlights.result: Incorporating astrometric jerk breaks the companion mass degeneracy inherent to acceleration alone, exhibiting power-law mass stratification $\log(|\ddot{\bm{r}}|)=\frac{4}{7}\log(|\dddot{\bm{r}}|)+\frac{1}{7}\log[G M_2^3 / (M_1+M_2)^2]$ for face-on circular binaries.
